newsitem.title: UK: S&P keeps British Gas Insurance rating on watch.
newsitem.headline: S&P keeps British Gas Insurance rating on watch.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday the AA minus claims paying ability of British Gas Insurance Company Ltd (BGI) remained on Creditwatch with developing implications.

"The rating was placed on Creditwatch on February 6, 1996 following the parent's announcement of its intention to demerge the gas supply business from the transmission business," S&P said in a statement.
"BGI's position within the proposed company structure has now been clarified - it will be owned by the transmission company, Transco International PLC," S&P said.
It said Transco was the regulated utility successor to British Gas and while taking on its debt obligations, was expected to have a stable credit profile.
"Since BGI is a captive insurer, the claims paying ability rating will therefore follow the rating ultimately assigned to Transco," the agency said.

S&P said BGI would be a slightly smaller concern but would continue to have very good financial strength based on low expenses, conservative underwriting, solid profitability, and strong capitalization.
S&P said it expected continued conservative management, strong profitability, and capitalization although business generated would continue to be tied to the Transco portfolio.
"Creditwatch resolution depends on settlement of current regulatory issues and successful demerger of British Gas PLC," S&P said.
S&P said the following ratings would be kept on Creditwatch devloping.
British Gas PLC
Senior debt AA minus
British Gas Finance Inc
Senior debt AA minus
British Gas International Finance B.V.
Senior debt AA minus
British Gas Insurance Company Ltd.
Claims Paying Ability AA minus
S&P also said the following ratings were on Creditwatch negative.
British Gas PLC
Commercial paper A1 plus
British Gas International Finance B.V.
Commercial paper A1 plus
British Gas Capital Inc
Commercial paper A1 plus
Major rating factors were as follows, S&P said.

- After the demerger, BGI would act as a captive insurer for Transco and would not write business for third parties. It would shed British Gas Energy Plc (BGE) business although it was likely that cover would continue to be provided for a short transitionary period while BGE established its own insurance arrangements.
S&P said it expected premium income to fall in 1997 as BGE premiums were lost but also as pricing became softer.
- A low expense base allowed BGI to offer very competitive insurance rates to the various business units of the parent company.

S&P expected the loss of BGE business to result in some increase in the expense ratio but that BGI would continue to be a very low cost provider and would generate considerable value to the parent company.
- Underwriting was strong, the key feature being the level of reinsurance protection with 32 percent of premiums reinsured.
"Coverage is provided by good quality insurers. However, there is some concentration risk in that 55 percent of business is placed with Lloyds," said S&P.

"The current arrangement extends over three years thereby locking in economical reinsurance protection for the medium term. A combination of low cost operations and strong underwriting is demonstrated by a combined ratio of 65 percent," S&P said.

- BGI has a relatively small capital base of 65 million stg, although increased from 38.1 million stg in 1994 as a result of profitable operations in 1995, and an addition to retained profit of 20 million stg brought about by the switch from three year to annual accounting, S&P said.
"Solvency is very high at 174 percent. S&P also considers BGI's capitalization to be impressive on a risk adjusted basis," the agency said.
"This may weaken slightly going forward because the company intends to alter its investment mix, switching some assets from cash to bonds, therefore taking on some degree of asset risk."
"Overall capitalization is expected to remain at excellent levels, however," S&P said.
